blocks.body: # CMU Panoptic 10-vs-3 Camera Study: Updated M2 Results

## Technical summary

All **1,175 synchronized moments** (**11,750 RGB frames**) were rerun from the same frozen M1 detections after one small M2 change. M2 now scores all reliable common joints instead of discarding limbs whenever two torso joints are visible. On the difficult band1 V10 run, pairwise F1 improves from **89.40%** to **99.82%**, wrong-person merge clusters fall from **46.27%** to **0.00%**, and MPJPE improves from **18.57** to **18.16 mm**.

With updated M2, pooled V10 MPJPE is **19.17 mm** versus **32.47 mm** for V3; joint availability is **100.00%** versus **91.51%**.

## Key findings

1. **The selected change is minimal:** M2 keeps the same calibration, epipolar geometry, confidence weighting, Hungarian matching, and 25 px gate; only the reliable joints entering the pair score change.
2. **It improves M2 F1 in all six sequence/condition runs.** The largest gain is band1 V10, the original failure case.
3. **It does not trade association for worse 3D output.** MPJPE improves in five of six runs; pose3 V10 changes by only +0.01 mm.
4. **Ten cameras still win the main comparison.** Every updated per-sequence bootstrap interval for V3−V10 MPJPE remains above zero.

## What changed, what was added, and why it helps

- **Changed:** the pair cost now uses every joint visible with sufficient confidence in both cameras. Previously, seeing two torso joints caused M2 to ignore the remaining joints.
- **Added:** one focused regression test and a frozen-detection ablation across gate tightening, stricter camera agreement, and the full-pose score. No learned component or extra inference stage was added.
- **Intuition:** two nearby people can have shoulders and hips near the same epipolar lines. Their elbows, wrists, knees, and ankles usually provide more distinctive geometric evidence. The confidence-weighted median remains robust to a few noisy limb joints.

Gate tightening and stricter camera agreement reduce some false links, but they also reject many correct links and split one person into multiple clusters. The full-pose score is the only tested option that sharply improves association while preserving or improving the final 3D result.
The V3−V10 gap remains positive in all sequences after the M2 update. Read MPJPE with availability because MPJPE averages only reconstructed eligible joints.
V10 reconstructs almost every eligible joint. Updated V3 gains a little coverage from cleaner association, but still loses the most joints in haggling1, where occlusion is strongest.

M2 pairwise F1 checks both cluster purity and recovery of correct same-person camera pairs. The updated score improves every run, including band1 V10 from 89.40% to 99.82%. GT person IDs are never used during inference; they are used only after clustering for this diagnostic.

## Scope, data, and metric definitions

The primary comparison uses the same M1 detections for V10 and V3 within each sequence. V10 uses cameras 50_01 through 50_10; V3 uses the fixed balanced subset 50_06, 50_04, and 50_02. Frames were sampled at stride 3, approximately 10 Hz. The three primary runs represent about **117.5 seconds** of sampled synchronized data.

- **MPJPE:** mean Euclidean error of reconstructed eligible 3D joints; lower is better.
- **PCK@50:** share of reconstructed joints within 50 mm; higher is better.
- **Joint availability:** reconstructed eligible joints divided by all eligible GT joints; higher is better.
- **Person precision/recall:** matching uses a 1,000 mm 3D gate. Precision penalizes extra predicted people; recall penalizes missed GT people.
- **M2 pairwise F1:** quality of same-person cross-camera clustering, evaluated with GT labels only after inference.
- **95% CI:** paired 2-second block bootstrap over frames, 2,000 iterations. A positive V3−V10 interval means V3 has higher error.

## Methodology

M1 is unchanged: RT-DETR-R50 detects people and ViTPose-Base predicts COCO-17 joints. M2 undistorts joints using CMU calibration. For every candidate pair, it measures symmetric epipolar distance for all joints scored at least 0.10 in both cameras, weights each distance by the geometric mean of the two joint confidences, and uses the weighted median as the pair cost. Camera-to-cluster costs remain the median across existing members; Hungarian assignment and the 25 px gate are unchanged.

M3 is unchanged: robust multiview triangulation uses a 12 px reprojection threshold, followed by refinement and 30 cm 3D duplicate suppression. Evaluation uses GT confidence >0.1 and paired 2-second block bootstrap intervals with 2,000 iterations.

## Limitations, uncertainty, and robustness

- The update was selected after inspecting performance on these three sequences, so a distinct held-out sequence is still needed to estimate generalization without selection bias.
- Only three sequences and about 117.5 seconds of synchronized data are included.
- V10 and V3 can reconstruct different joint sets; availability must remain beside MPJPE and PCK.
- Haggling1 has 285 paired bootstrap frames although 300 moments were processed; its interval uses the common evaluable subset.
- The method remains geometry-only with 0 learned M2 parameters; it can still struggle when multiple people have similar poses along ambiguous epipolar lines.

## Complete artifact inventory

The inventory now includes the three updated full-pose reruns and the Band1 V10 ablations. Repeated ablations use the same 575 moments and are not added to the 1,175-moment primary total.

## Data-quality audit

The updated evaluation reuses the validated M1 caches and GT assignment files. Every updated V10 and V3 output has exactly one row per source moment (575, 300, and 300), and all six evaluations completed.

## Recommended next steps

1. Freeze the full-pose score as the default M2 pathway.
2. Validate it on a new crowded sequence not used to choose the method.
3. Only add a more complex cue—appearance or temporal consistency—if that held-out test exposes a remaining failure that geometry cannot resolve.

## Further questions

- Does the improvement hold on an unseen crowded sequence?
- Which limb joints contribute most to resolving close-person ambiguity?
- Can the same full-pose score improve arbitrary three-camera subsets, not only the fixed balanced V3 subset?
